coverage_notes: Swept across three major angles: (1) MARKET SIZING & ANALYST REPORTS covering data visualization ($19.2B by 2027, 10.2% CAGR), low-code/no-code ($44.5B in 2026, 19% CAGR), graph databases ($5.6B by 2028, 22.3% CAGR), RAG tools ($4.18B in 2026, 25.7% CAGR), knowledge graphs ($3.5B in 2026 → $19.6B by 2035, 21.1% CAGR), vector databases ($10.6B by 2032, 27.5% CAGR), workflow automation ($26B in 2026 → $40.77B by 2031), and enterprise knowledge management. (2) COMPETITIVE BUSINESS MODELS examining Retool/Budibase (creator+user pricing, freemium models), Neo4j (consumption + enterprise licensing), Tableau/Power BI/Looker (per-seat vs usage-based), Snowflake/Databricks (cloud consumption model), and emerging vertical SaaS patterns (11% lower churn, 49% faster growth via embedded workflows). (3) ENTERPRISE BUYING BEHAVIOR & PRICING STRATEGIES including SaaS tiers (hybrid models winning at 70% preference by 2026), B2B buyer adoption (60%+ use trials, AI discovery, peer communities driving 65% of searches), IT budget allocation (28-32% personnel, 26-30% SaaS, 20-24% infrastructure), and platform convergence trends (AI agents, semantic search, data platform consolidation). Deduped across 400+ search results to ~40 unique high-tier sources. Named authorities: Gartner (market forecasts, magic quadrants, peer insights), Forrester (enterprise predictions, spending forecasts), Fortune Business Insights, Precedence Research, MarketsandMarkets, Grand View Research (CAGR/sizing). Notable gaps: no specific MetroGraph product pages found (repo may be private/early); limited detail on competitor 9-block BMCs (inferred from business model fragments); no deep-dive on Angular 17 + SignalDB technical moat analysis (found frameworks separately). Coverage weighted T0 (Gartner/Forrester forecasts, pricing pages) → T1 (official docs, analyst platforms) → T2 (market research reports, aggregates) → T3 (practitioner guides, comparison blogs).
